name: Münster
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village in the Inntal with a beautiful Kirchenburg and stunning hikes up its Hausberg.
text:
Overview

Münster is situated in the Tyrolean Unterinntal on a sunny alluvial terrace at 534 meters above sea level, approximately 38 kilometers northeast of Innsbruck and eight kilometers west of Kramsach. Located in the Kufstein district, this welcoming community is home to roughly 3,500 residents and extends from the north bank of the Inn River up to the sheer southern crags of the Rofan mountains. Münster benefits from a sheltered southern exposure, granting the village one of the highest annual sunshine tallies in the entire Inn valley. Münster is widely known across Austria as a premier health center, anchored by the state-of-the-art Rehabilitation Centre Münster. The town brings together a lively civic community, peaceful natural spaces, and direct trailheads into high-alpine climbing and hiking routes.

History

Human settlement around Münster began centuries before documented history, but the earliest recorded mention dates back to around 1140–1150 as 'Munsteren'. The name derives from the Latin term 'monasterium', indicating an early monastic foundation or proprietary church. For generations, local livelihoods depended on alpine farming, timber harvesting, and timber rafting along the Inn. Thanks to its elevated position on an alluvial fan, the historic village center remained protected from recurring severe river floods. The parish church of the Assumption (Mariä Himmelfahrt) features a prominent late Gothic spire and was sumptuously decorated in the late 18th century with Rococo stuccoes and colorful ceiling frescoes. During the late 20th century, Münster evolved from a farming hamlet into an attractive residential community and a celebrated center for medical rehabilitation and wellness.

Getting There

Münster boasts excellent transport connections by road and rail. By car, motorists take the A12 Inntal Autobahn, exiting at Wiesing/Zillertal (coming from the west) or Kramsach (coming from the east), followed by a brief drive along the B171 Tiroler Straße straight into town. By train, visitors can take the Tyrolean S-Bahn (lines S4 and S5) to the Münster-Wiesing station, or use the nearby railway junctions at Brixlegg or Jenbach, where faster regional express trains stop regularly. Frequent VVT regional buses connect the railway hubs with all residential quarters and the rehabilitation clinic. Cyclists can also reach Münster effortlessly along the celebrated Inn River Cycle Path (Inn-Radweg).

Tips

Münster is a hidden gem for tranquility seekers and mountaineers alike. An acclaimed hike leads up to the historic Bayreuther Hütte alpine refuge at 1,576 meters, offering breathtaking panoramic vistas across the Inn valley toward the Zillertal Alps, with summit routes continuing to the Sonnwendjoch (2,224 m). For an easier excursion, walk to the enchanting Hauserer See, a secluded forest pond wrapped in serene quietude. Another delightful stroll follows the protected Münsterer Inn-Auen riparian woodlands along the river, rich in native flora and birdlife. Patients and visitors will also appreciate the therapeutic spa gardens of the Münster Rehabilitation Centre, offering paved paths, sensory gardens, and sweeping mountain panoramas.
